classification.difficultyReason: Calculate slopes and intercepts for three supplied line segments and assign domain intervals with consistent endpoint inclusion.

content.prompt: Specify the function represented by this graph:

spec.description: Connected red line segments through (-3,0), (-1,2), (2,-1) and (4,-2), with filled outer endpoints, unit ticks and labelled axes. No grid.
spec.mathematics: y=x+3 on [-3,-1]; y=-x+1 on [-1,2]; y=-x/2 on [2,4]. Adjacent rules agree at both internal vertices.
spec.answerVisibility: Student-visible supplied graph; no equations displayed.

answer.worked:
For the segment from $(-3,0)$ to $(-1,2)$:
$$\begin{aligned}m&=\frac{2-0}{-1-(-3)}\\&=1,\\0&=-3+b,\\b&=3.\end{aligned}$$
For the segment from $(-1,2)$ to $(2,-1)$:
$$\begin{aligned}m&=\frac{-1-2}{2-(-1)}\\&=-1,\\2&=1+b,\\b&=1.\end{aligned}$$
For the segment from $(2,-1)$ to $(4,-2)$:
$$\begin{aligned}m&=\frac{-2-(-1)}{4-2}\\&=-\frac12,\\-1&=-1+b,\\b&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The filled outer endpoints are included. At each internal vertex, the adjacent rules give the same value; assign that vertex to one interval:
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}x+3,&-3\le x\le-1,\\-x+1,&-1<x\le2,\\-\dfrac{x}{2},&2<x\le4.\end{cases}$$
